experiment: Vol.2 · A2 (Nemotron 3 Nano, NIM 2.0.12, NVFP4) · at cap 256 and a fixed concurrency, does lowering only the CUDA-graph capture size to what cap 32 implies slow the engine? Two containers in one run, profile C, levels 1, 16, 32
written_before: the measured run. run_p55_capture_control.sh refuses to start if this file or its .sha256 is missing or changed, or if levels.jsonl exists.
why: p55_concurrency_a2_{256,128} and p53_concurrency_v2 (cap 32) measured profile C at the same concurrency with rates rising with the cap: c=32 1,540 / 1,738 / 2,238 tok/s, p50 ITL 19.4 / 17.5 / 13.6 ms at caps 32 / 128 / 256 (cap 64, run later: 1,130); c=1 equal (283-300). vLLM 0.27.1 sets the largest CUDA-graph capture size to min(2 x max_num_seqs, 512) tokens (vllm/config/vllm.py _set_cudagraph_sizes); the startup logs captured 11 / 35 / 51 mixed prefill-decode sizes and 7 / 19 / 35 decode sizes at caps 32 / 128 / 256. A step with a 200-token prompt joining ~30 decodes (~230 tokens) is above the cap-32 capture limit (64) and below the cap-256 one (512). Main and fresh containers of one configuration differed by up to 31% at c=64 in the same sweeps, so the reference is measured in this run, back to back, and only the capture size changes. A harness test on 2026-09-23 22:25 (condition s256_cg064, c=1, 20 s) showed the setting reaches the engine (11 mixed and 11 decode sizes captured) and the analyser reading it from real rows. Added by the lab without a ticket (same question as P55 G1, under 30 minutes of GPU), reported as an autonomous addition.
not_run: the reverse direction (cap 32 with the cap-256 capture size): kept under the 30-minute limit for an addition without a ticket
as_p55_concurrency_a2: image, profile, NIM_MAX_MODEL_LEN, AIPerf flags, discarded 120 s warm-up level, calibration, engine-death detection, level durations, log saving: imported unchanged (p53_concurrency_v2.py). Levels 1, 16, 32; main container only (no fresh repeat: levels at or below the cap-32 value, where main and fresh agreed within 3.5% in p53_concurrency_v2)
note: control arms, not A2's configuration; they do not replace any concurrency result

analysis_rules.program: vol2/scripts/p55_capture_control_analyze.py (8 self-test cases; mutations of the verdict thresholds and the capture rule each fail one case; run on the harness test's real rows)
analysis_rules.preconditions: per condition: P1 every measured level clean; P2 calibration max(20 ms, 20%) TTFT and 20% ITL at c=1; P3 the startup log's mixed prefill-decode capture count equals the setting's (default at cap 256 -> 51, 64 -> 11)
analysis_rules.verdict: r = s256_cg064 / s256_default, output tok/s at c=32, both from this run (r16 at c=16 beside it). measured: r <= 0.85; withdrawn: r >= 0.95; partial otherwise; unverified if a precondition fails

predictions.basis: the three sweeps above; A1's CUDA-graph control (p55_a1_capture) found removing graphs costs 31% per decode step at ~4k tokens on that engine
predictions.R1: both conditions apply the capture setting (P3 holds)
predictions.R2: verdict 'measured': r <= 0.85 (the capture size alone moves c=32 toward the cap-32 rate)
predictions.R3: at c=1 the two conditions are within 5% of each other (single stream is inside every capture list)
predictions.R4: s256_default at c=32 is within 15% of the sweep's 2,238 tok/s
predictions.confidence: R1 high, R2 medium, R3 high, R4 medium
predictions.reading: a failed R is reported as failed
